_decision: onDarkDisabled = oklch(0.42 0 0). the icon colour of the permanently disabled Profile button. The value comes from proposedDarkRailTokens — the approved decision record — NOT from measuring the component and writing down what it happened to say. If this check fails, that is the finding.
_serialisation: The expected string is the COMPUTED spelling. tokens.css authors some colours as oklch(55.6% 0 0) while the browser computes oklch(0.556 0 0) — the same colour, and compare() is exact string equality. proposedDarkRailTokens already uses the computed spelling, so the value is copied unchanged. Never resolve a mismatch by pasting the measured value.
_scope: state is `rest`, not `disabled`, deliberately: this element IS disabled, so rest and disabled render identically here. The runner does not simulate `disabled` either — it requires an already-disabled element, which this is. Forcing it would measure a state the component may never enter.
_audit_finding: The Independent Audit found this check certified the DECLARATION, not the colour. Two agents on different lenses found it and it was re-measured directly: the element computes color oklch(0.42 0 0) AND opacity 0.5, from Button's own `disabled:opacity-50` (src/ui/button.tsx). getComputedStyle().color cannot see opacity — they are separate compositing properties — so the glyph a human sees is that colour at half strength over the rail's oklch(0.205 0 0), roughly rgb(50,50,50). The check passed while measuring a colour that is never painted.
_resolution: RESOLVED by the owner after the Independent Audit surfaced it. The token was never wrong — `opacity-50` was applying the disabled treatment a SECOND time on top of a token that already carried it, so the approved oklch(0.42 0 0) painted as rgb(50,50,50) instead. `Button`'s `disabled:opacity-50` is suppressed for this one element via `disabled:opacity-100` and the token now paints at full strength. `disabled:pointer-events-none` deliberately remains: the suppression is the opacity only, never the disabled behaviour.
_why_opacity_is_asserted: `opacity: 1` is asserted alongside the colour and is the load-bearing half. Without it this check passes on a correct `color` while the glyph paints at any strength — which is exactly how it passed before. If Button's base recipe ever reaches this element again, the colour assertion will not notice and this one will.
_cascade_fragility: Measured in the compiled stylesheet, not assumed: `disabled:opacity-50` BEATS `disabled:opacity-100` regardless of class order — a disabled element carrying both computes 0.5 whether written '50 then 100' or '100 then 50'. The suppression therefore rests entirely on tailwind-merge DELETING the base class, not on the cascade. If both ever reach the element — a nested merge, a `cn()` call that concatenates instead of merging, a Button variant change — it silently reverts to the double-applied value with no error. The `opacity: "1"` assertion here is the only thing that would notice, which is why it is not decoration.
